newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - P&G pact boosts Regeneron's cash.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - P&G pact boosts Regeneron's cash.

text.p: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc's drug discovery collaboration with Procter & Gamble Co gives the biotechnology company the cash to expand its research efforts, although it doesn't guarantee that products will actually come to market.

"This is by far the largest transaction that we have entered into and the broadest. In addition to technology synergies, it provides the financial wherewithal to conduct research," said Leonard Schleifer, Regeneron's president and chief executive officer in a telephone interview Tuesday.

Earlier in the day, Procter & Gamble said it would pay Regeneron $135 million over five years as part of a collaboration to discover, develop and commercialize pharmaceutical products with applictions to cardiovascular, bone, muscle, arthritis and other areas.
Regeneron stock soared 4-1/8 to 12 in late afternoon trade on the news.
"This makes Rgeneron much more viable in the next few years," said Kenneth Pounds, senior biotechnology analyst with Nutmeg Securities.

"There aren't any near-term prospects for drugs in the market after the BDNF failure. This makes it more likely that the company will survive to a day that they will have a drug on the market," he said.
Regenron is also in a collaboration with Amgen Inc to develop Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) as a treatment for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, also known as ALS, or Lou Gehrig's disease.
In January, Amgen and Regeneron said that a Phase BDNF trial failed to show clinical efficacy of the drug when administered by regular, subcutaneous injection.
The companies are continuing to study the the efficacy of BDNF when delivered directly into the patient's spinal fluid.
But Pounds warned that just because Regeneron is getting help to defray expenses and lower its cash burn rate, the funding does not assure that a product will actually make it to the market.
"Now Regeneron can expand research efforts. With expansion, the odds of hitting a homerun in about five years are increased -- but it doesn't improve the odds to a huge extent," he said.

P&G will take close to a 20 percent equity stake in the 31 million shares Regeneron will have outstanding after issuing new shares as part of the deal. Regeneron currently has about 26 million shares outstanding.
"Procter & Gamble saw in us the possibility of filling their pipeline. They bring both the development capability and strength in marketing and sales," said Roy Vagelos, chairman of Regeneron.

James Schwartz, a spokeman for Procter & Gamble said that the current focus area of its pharmaceutical division, which has annual sales of about $500 million, are in the cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and antiinfective area.
"We believe there is synergy with two of the three of our focus areas," Schwartz told Reuters.
But Pounds said he was surprised at the deal.

"P&G is really going against the trend of large corporations concentrating on their core businesses," he said. Investing in biotechnology is very risky and difficult. The area has a poor record of success."
Procter & Gamble shares fell 1-1/4 to 132-1/2 in late afternoon trade.
